title: Signature Chain Provenance Ledger
description: Signature edition: every link execution in the chain is recorded in a provenance ledger — prompt version, model identity, inputs hash, outputs hash, human approvals. Any chain run can be replayed bit-for-bit or audited link by link, years later. This is a Signature original method.
method: The orchestrator hashes each link's I/O and appends a ledger entry; replay feeds recorded outputs back instead of calling models.
usage: Enable the ledger on all production chains; use replay for debugging and audits.

demo.code:
import hashlib
ledger = []
for link, out in [('outline', 'o1'), ('draft', 'd1')]:
    h = hashlib.sha256(out.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    ledger.append((link, h))
    print(f'ledger: {link} -> {h}')
print('replay: feed recorded outputs, zero model calls')

title: Signature Branching and routing chains
description: Signature edition: Real workflows branch: a router prompt classifies the input and sends it down different sub-chains (refund request -> billing chain; bug report -> engineering chain). Routing keeps each chain specialized instead of one chain handling everything badly.
method: A classifier link outputs a route label; the orchestrator dispatches to the matching sub-chain; results merge at a join link.
usage: Define routes explicitly with examples; add a default route for unclassifiable inputs.

demo.code:
routes = {'billing': 'billing-chain', 'bug': 'eng-chain'}
req = 'my invoice is wrong'
route = 'billing' if 'invoice' in req else 'bug'
print(f'input: {req!r} -> route: {route} -> {routes[route]}')

title: Signature Conditional retry with fallback prompts
description: Signature edition: When a link's output fails validation, the chain doesn't crash — it retries with a fallback prompt (simpler instructions, a different model, or a repair prompt showing the error). Retries are bounded, and persistent failure routes to a human or a safe default.
method: Validate link output; on failure, retry with the repair prompt (original output + error); after k failures, escalate or use the fallback value.
usage: Make validators strict and repair prompts specific; alert on repeated link failures (a prompt bug, not bad luck).

demo.code:
attempts = ['bad json {', '{"ok": true}']
for i, out in enumerate(attempts):
    ok = out.startswith('{') and out.endswith('}')
    print(f'attempt {i+1}: {"valid" if ok else "invalid -> repair prompt"}')

title: Signature Self-critique revision loops
description: Signature edition: The chain generates a draft, then a critic prompt scores it against a rubric and lists flaws, then a reviser fixes them — looping until the critic is satisfied or iterations run out. Draft-critique-revise turns one-shot generation into hill-climbing toward quality.
method: Generate -> critique (rubric scores + flaw list) -> revise addressing flaws; repeat; stop on score threshold or max iterations; keep the best-scoring version.
usage: Write the critic rubric carefully — the loop optimizes exactly what the critic measures.

demo.code:
draft, score = 'v1 draft', 6.0
for i in range(2):
    score += 1.5
    print(f'iteration {i+1}: critic score {score:.1f} -> revise')
print('final: best version kept (score 9.0)')

title: Signature Chain versioning and A/B testing
description: Signature edition: Prompts are code: chains get versioned (v1.2.3), and traffic splits between versions to measure which performs better on real inputs. Winning versions graduate; losers are kept for rollback. Prompt engineering becomes an experiment, not an argument.
method: Version every prompt template; route a fraction of traffic to the challenger; compare on logged metrics (task success, latency, cost); promote or roll back.
usage: Change one link at a time in challengers so wins are attributable; keep rollback one click away.

title: Signature Streaming chain observability
description: Signature edition: Long chains are black boxes unless instrumented: every link streams its inputs, outputs, token counts, latency, and cost to a trace viewer. When a chain misbehaves in production, the trace shows exactly which link went wrong and what it saw.
method: Wrap each link execution in a span (trace id, link name, timing, tokens, cost); stream spans to the observability backend; render as a waterfall.
usage: Always trace in production (sample if volume is huge); alert on link-level latency or cost anomalies.

demo.code:
spans = [('outline', 1200, 1.2), ('draft', 3400, 4.1), ('polish', 800, 0.6)]
for name, ms, cost in spans:
    print(f'  {name:8} {ms}ms  ${cost:.2f}')
print('trace complete: 3 links, 5.4s, $5.90')

title: Signature Map-reduce over document sets
description: Signature edition: For long inputs, the chain maps over chunks (summarize each section independently, in parallel) then reduces (combine section summaries into one). Map-reduce chains process arbitrarily long documents with bounded context per call.
method: Split input into chunks; map link runs per chunk in parallel; reduce link merges partial results, possibly hierarchically for very long inputs.
usage: Size chunks to leave headroom for the prompt; reduce hierarchically if partial results overflow context.

demo.code:
chunks = ['sec1 text', 'sec2 text', 'sec3 text']
partials = [f'summary({c})' for c in chunks]
print('mapped:', partials)
print('reduced: combined summary of 3 sections')

title: Signature ReAct interleaved reasoning-acting
description: Signature edition: ReAct alternates Thought, Action, Observation: the model reasons about what to do, calls a tool, observes the result, and reasons again. This loop grounds chains in real tool outputs instead of letting the model hallucinate intermediate results.
method: Prompt the model to emit Thought/Action/Action-Input triples; the runtime executes the action, appends the Observation, and loops until a Final Answer or step limit.
usage: Give the model a small, well-described toolset; cap steps; log every thought/action pair.

demo.code:
trace = [('Thought', 'need the price'), ('Action', 'lookup(sku-1)'), ('Observation', '$12.99')]
for kind, text in trace:
    print(f'{kind:11}: {text}')
print('Final Answer: The price is $12.99')

title: Signature Human-in-the-loop checkpoints
description: Signature edition: For consequential chains, the workflow pauses at checkpoints and waits for a human to approve, edit, or reject the intermediate output before continuing. The chain becomes a collaboration: the model drafts, the human decides, the model continues.
method: Mark links as gated; on reaching a gate, the orchestrator persists state and notifies the human; resume applies the human's edited output as the link result.
usage: Gate high-stakes links (external sends, irreversible actions); keep low-stakes links automatic.

demo.code:
state = {'draft': 'Send refund of $50'}
print('CHECKPOINT: draft =', state['draft'])
human = 'approved with edit: $55'
print('human:', human, '-> chain resumes')
